name: Bukki
overview: Bukki was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known as the son of Abishua and the father of Uzzi. He belonged to the Aaronic priestly lineage through Eleazar, serving as a link in the hereditary priesthood. His role within the tribe of Levi highlights his importance in the religious leadership of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Bukki means 'proved of y-h-v-h' or 'mouth [gurgle sounds] of y-h-v-h,' reflecting a connection to the Lord. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 6:5, is not indicated as given directly by God but carries significant meaning related to his identity and service.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Bukki as the son of Abishua and the father of Uzzi, establishing his place in a priestly family line. These relationships are explicitly noted in 1 Chronicles 6:5, underscoring the continuity of the Aaronic priesthood through his lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Bukki holds significance as a key figure in the Aaronic priestly succession, linking Eleazar’s descendants in the service of God. His mention in 1 Chronicles 6:5 situates him within the sacred heritage entrusted with maintaining the spiritual duties of Israel. Through Bukki, the priestly lineage is preserved, emphasizing God's faithfulness in sustaining the leadership of His people.
